Beerothite
bee-EH-roth-ite
proper noun (gentilic)
Hebrew Beerothi (H886), an inhabitant of Beeroth, one of the four Gibeonite cities; from beer (H875), a well.

Biblical Definition

Beeroth was one of the four cities of the Gibeonites who obtained a league with Joshua by pretending to come from a far country, and it was afterwards reckoned to Benjamin. Its people are named in two very different connections. The first is a crime: the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin — Baanah and Rechab, captains of Ishbosheth's bands — came about the heat of the day to the house of their master, who lay on a bed at noon, and murdered him in his bed, and carried his head to David at Hebron expecting a reward (2Sa 4:2, 5). David's answer was to name the deed for what it was and execute them. The second is honourable: Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah, is listed among the thirty (2Sa 23:37). The same small town produced two regicides and one of the king's mighty men. The parenthesis in the record is its own quiet note: the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day (2Sa 4:3).

Origin & Era

An inhabitant of Beeroth, a Gibeonite city reckoned to Benjamin; the murderers of Ishbosheth were Beerothites, and so was Naharai, armourbearer to Joab.

BEEROTHITE, Hebrew Beerothi, an inhabitant of Beeroth; from beer, a well.

Beeroth was one of the four cities of the Gibeonites, afterwards reckoned to Benjamin.

Baanah and Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, were captains of Ishbosheth's bands.

They slew their master upon his bed at noon and carried his head to David.

Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab, was among David's mighty men.

Key Scripture

2Sa 4:2 — "And Saul's son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:"

2Sa 4:3 — "And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)"

2Sa 4:5 — "And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon."

2Sa 23:37 — "Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,"

Modern Corruption

Serving a good cause is taken to sanctify the deed; David executed the men who murdered his rival in bed and expected thanks.

expand to see more

Baanah and Rechab had read the political situation correctly. Abner was dead, Ishbosheth's cause was collapsing, David was certain to reign over all Israel, and the LORD had said so. They removed the last obstacle and brought the head to Hebron with a piece of theology attached: the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed (2Sa 4:8). Every clause of their reasoning about the outcome was true. David had them killed, and told them why: when one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead… I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag… How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? (2Sa 4:10-11).

This is the standing refusal of Scripture to let a good end launder a wicked means. Paul states it as a question and answers it with the strongest negative in the Greek: Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just (Rom 3:8). Uzzah steadied the ark with the best of intentions. Saul spared the Amalekite cattle to sacrifice them. The principle to recover is that God does not need our sins to accomplish His promises, and that a man who commits one in the service of a cause he is sure God favours has still committed it, and will answer for it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Beerothi (H886), from Beeroth (H881), wells, a Gibeonite city; from beer (H875), a well.

expand to see more

Hebrew beer (H875) — a well, a pit dug for water; the root of the place-name.

Hebrew Beeroth (H881) — Beeroth, one of the four cities of the Gibeonites (Jos 9:17).

Hebrew Beerothi (H886) — a Beerothite; 2 Samuel 4:2, 4:3, 4:5, 4:9, 23:37.

Hebrew Ishbosheth (H378) — man of shame; the son of Saul murdered upon his bed.

Hebrew tsaddiq (H6662) — a righteous person; wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house (2Sa 4:11).

Usage

"“The sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin”."

"“The Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day”."

"“Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah”."
